reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, full StructureDefinition report, direct HTTP behavior finding, shared behavior context, R4/R6 package StructureDefinitions, and R4 maturity context. Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were treated as context only. The deterministic aggregate was compared only after forming the resource-level conclusion.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured` is trial-use/FMM 0, so the baseline compatibility burden is weak. That lowers objections to a substantial R6 redesign, but it does not erase the regulatory/product-traceability value of preserving low-cost compatibility for resource identity and mandatory quantity data.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 replaces `MedicinalProductManufactured` with `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, so a migration program is unavoidable, but old identity aliases and preservation of mandatory R4 `quantity` would still be high-value compatibility work.

reasoning.thesisMd: `MedicinalProductManufactured` is not a mostly stable resource with a few local edits. The R4 resource identity is absent in R6 and the apparent successor is `ManufacturedItemDefinition`; existing instances, canonical references, generated models, REST endpoint inventories, and validators must be transformed. Several element changes then require policy decisions rather than simple field copies.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The practical migration shape is a resource replacement plus model remodel. Retained concepts such as `manufacturedDoseForm`, `unitOfPresentation`, and `manufacturer` remain recognizable, but R6 adds mandatory modifier `status`, removes mandatory root `quantity`, changes `ingredient` from references to coded/inbound `Ingredient` patterns, and remodels physical/other characteristics into generic `property` entries. That makes resource-level migration unavoidable even before considering shared base behavior.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The identity break lowers the value of preserving every old element name in isolation, because R4 payloads cannot validate until the resource type and related references are rewritten. It does not make compatibility preservation pointless. Retaining the old resource identity as a deprecated alias or retaining a deprecated optional `quantity` would preserve large compatibility surfaces at comparatively modest model cost, so the posture is to preserve low-cost compatibility while expecting a migration program.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most standards-review-worthy alternatives are: keep `MedicinalProductManufactured` as the resource type/canonical while using metadata aliases for the clearer R6 name, and keep a deprecated optional root `quantity` with explicit relationship rules to component, constituent, or packaging quantities. Making `status` optional would reduce breakage but would weaken lifecycle filtering too much. Keeping old ingredient references or old physical-characteristic fields would reduce local migration work but risks duplicate or conflicting composition/characteristic representations. Optional R6 additions need down-conversion guidance, not a less-breaking base design.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct HTTP behavior finding confirms that the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises the R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured` endpoint. That is a real runtime/discovery concern, but it is derivative of the resource replacement rather than an independent model break. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` operation and search findings may affect generic migration tooling, but they are context only for this assigned resource.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the aggregate on `removed-or-replaced-resource`, `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable: Yes`, and the high-confidence need for a migration program. I differ slightly on compatibility leverage: the aggregate chose `migration-program-dominates`, while this review chooses `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration` because the resource identity and mandatory `quantity` findings remain avoidable or low-cost-to-preserve enough to warrant standards attention.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The successor identification is high confidence from local package evidence, `fhir-old-types`, and matching retained elements. Exact element mapping confidence is lower because the local inputs lack an official R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, narrative migration page, and terminology expansions for product characteristics and ingredients.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 MedicinalProductManufactured resource is absent in R6 and appears renamed/replaced by ManufacturedItemDefinition
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the primary migration-shape finding. It breaks `resourceType`, canonical StructureDefinition URLs, generated classes, references, and REST/API routing. Even with FMM 0, the old identity appears preserveable through metadata/title/alias choices rather than a new wire identity, so it remains standards-review-worthy.

findingConsiderations.title: Mandatory R4 quantity has no direct R6 successor element
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Every valid R4 instance had `quantity`, and R6 has no root successor. Dropping or inventing this value can affect packaging, labeling, count, and regulatory traceability. A deprecated optional compatibility field or explicit base mapping looks lower cost than silent loss, so this finding materially affects the compatibility-leverage conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 successor adds mandatory modifier status with a required publication-status binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is an old-valid/new-invalid break after resource rewrite, and migrations must not blindly default all historical items to `active`. Still, lifecycle status is central to a definition resource and the required value set includes `unknown`, so it is a local migration chore rather than a reason to reject the R6 redesign.

findingConsiderations.title: Ingredient changed from references to R4 MedicinalProductIngredient into coded/inbound R6 Ingredient patterns
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Ingredient migration is safety- and regulatory-relevant and requires graph-level mapping with the separate `Ingredient` resource. Once the broader R6 ingredient model is accepted, however, preserving the old outward reference list in the same base resource risks duplicate/conflicting composition facts, so this is mainly a high-care migration chore.

findingConsiderations.title: Physical and other characteristics are remodeled from typed R4 fields into generic R6 property entries
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The remodel breaks generated accessors and requires a property-type mapping table for color, imprint, dimensions, image, scoring, and other characteristics. The flexible property model is plausible for low-maturity content, so this should drive migration guidance and terminology mapping rather than resource-level compatibility veto.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 successor adds optional identifier, name, marketing status, and component hierarchy not present in R4
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These additions are optional and do not make R4-derived instances invalid. They matter for R6-to-R4 down-conversion and round trips, but they are ordinary forward-compatible model enrichment rather than an avoidable R4-to-R6 break.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `MedicinalProductManufactured` is among the affected resources, so clients that derive route inventories from the base CapabilityStatement will lose the old endpoint. This supports the need for endpoint transition guidance or aliases, but it is derivative of the resource replacement decision.

findingConsiderations.title: Required input parameter renamed from `input` to `resource`
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior changes, including `$convert`, `$meta`, `$validate`, and special search parameter metadata, can affect generic cross-version tooling. They are not specific to `MedicinalProductManufactured` and therefore were not scored as direct resource-level migration drivers.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or verify an official R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured` to R6 `ManufacturedItemDefinition` migration map covering resource type, canonical URL, references, endpoint/search replacement guidance, and profile/package allow-list updates.

Revisit the dropped mandatory R4 `quantity`: either retain a deprecated optional root compatibility element or provide an official base mapping/extension with clear rules for relation to component, constituent, and packaging quantities.

Define product-domain migration rules for `status`, ingredient graph conversion, and characteristic `property` coding; include tests that prevent unsafe status defaults and ingredient/characteristic data loss.

Add CapabilityStatement/API transition guidance for old `MedicinalProductManufactured` endpoints and generated clients, including whether deprecated endpoint aliases are expected, forbidden, or implementation-specific.

caveats: No official local ConceptMap or narrative R4-to-R6 migration note was available.
R4 FMM 0/trial-use means broad production impact should not be assumed from the break alone.
Terminology expansions for ingredient and characteristic mappings were not available locally.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed only as context for generic tooling.
